bottom_line: In patients with severe heart failure, spironolactone vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality (relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82).
implications: In this trial of severe heart failure, spironolactone (25 mg daily, with protocolized dose adjustments) vs placebo was associated with fewer deaths (46 percent vs 35 percent; relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001) and fewer cardiac hospitalizations (336/753 vs 260/515; relative risk, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.59 to 0.82; P<0.001). The document also reports increased gynecomastia or breast pain in men (10 percent vs 1 percent; P<0.001) and low reported serious hyperkalemia in both groups (1 percent vs 2 percent). These results are reported for the enrolled population under the stated eligibility/exclusion criteria and follow-up duration, and do not by themselves establish effects outside those criteria.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized comparison of spironolactone 25 mg daily vs placebo.
major_points.quote:
patients were randomly assigned in
a double-blind fashion to receive either 25 mg of spironolactone
(Aldactone, Searle, Skokie, Ill.) once daily or a matching placebo.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was death from any cause and was analyzed by intention-to-treat.
major_points.quote: The primary end point of the study was death from any cause.

major_points.text: The trial was stopped early after interim analysis showed efficacy for all-cause mortality.
major_points.quote:
at the fifth planned in-
terim analysis, the observed effect of spironolactone
on the risk of death from all causes exceeded the
prespecified critical z value. Hence, the trial was
stopped on August 24, 1998

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with spironolactone than placebo.
major_points.quote:
There were 386 deaths in the placebo
group (46 percent) and 284 in the spironolactone
group (35 percent; relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 per-
cent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Gynecomastia or breast pain was more common among men assigned spironolactone.
major_points.quote:
Gynecomastia or breast pain was reported
in 10 percent of men who were treated with spirono-
lactone, as compared with 1 percent of men in the
placebo group (P<0.001).

absolute_effects.text: Deaths: placebo 386 (46 percent) vs spironolactone 284 (35 percent).
absolute_effects.quote:
There were 386 deaths in the placebo
group (46 percent) and 284 in the spironolactone
group (35 percent; relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 per-
cent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001).

absolute_effects.text: Deaths from cardiac causes: placebo 314 (37 percent) vs spironolactone 226 (27 percent).
absolute_effects.quote:
A total of 314 deaths in the placebo group (37
percent) and 226 deaths in the spironolactone group
(27 percent) were attributed to cardiac causes

absolute_effects.text: Hospitalized at least once for cardiac reasons: placebo 336 vs spironolactone 260.
absolute_effects.quote:
During the trial, 336 patients in the placebo group
and 260 patients in the spironolactone group were
hospitalized at least once for cardiac reasons

absolute_effects.text: Hospitalizations for cardiac causes: placebo 753 vs spironolactone 515.
absolute_effects.quote:
In total, there were 753 hospitalizations for car-
diac causes in the placebo group and 515 in the
spironolactone group

subgroups.text: Effect assessed using six prerandomization variables (prespecified).
subgroups.quote:
The effect of spironolactone was also
assessed with the use of six prerandomization variables: left ven-
tricular ejection fraction, the cause of heart failure, the serum cre-
atinine concentration, age, the use of ACE inhibitors, and the use
of digitalis.

subgroups.text: Reduction in risk of death was similar in analyses of all six prespecified subgroups.
subgroups.quote:
The reduction in the risk of death among patients
in the spironolactone group was similar in analyses
of all six prespecified subgroups

subgroups.text: Retrospective analyses were performed according to sex, NYHA class, baseline potassium, potassium supplements, and beta-blocker use.
subgroups.quote:
as well as in retro-
spective analyses performed according to sex, NYHA
class, base-line serum potassium concentration, use
of potassium supplements, and use of beta-blockers

harms.text: Serious hyperkalemia occurred in 10 placebo patients (1%) and 14 spironolactone patients (2%).
Discontinuation because of adverse event occurred in 5% with placebo and 8% with spironolactone.

inclusion_criteria.text: NYHA class IV heart failure within the prior 6 months and NYHA class III or IV at enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
Patients were eligible for enrollment if they had had New York
Heart Association (NYHA) class IV heart failure within the six
months before enrollment and were in NYHA class III or IV at
the time of enrollment

inclusion_criteria.text: Diagnosis of heart failure at least 6 weeks before enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
had been given a diagnosis of heart failure
at least six weeks before enrollment

inclusion_criteria.text: Treated with an ACE inhibitor (if tolerated) and a loop diuretic.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
were being treated with an
ACE inhibitor (if tolerated) and a loop diuretic

inclusion_criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction no more than 35 percent within 6 months before enrollment.
inclusion_criteria.quote:
had a left
ventricular ejection fraction of no more than 35 percent within
the six months before enrollment

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum creatinine concentration of more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (221 µmol per liter).
exclusion_criteria.quote:

criteria for exclusion were a serum creatinine concentration of
more than 2.5 mg per deciliter (221 µmol per liter)

exclusion_criteria.text: Serum potassium concentration of more than 5.0 mmol per liter.

analysis_methods.text: Primary analysis included all patients by intention-to-treat.
analysis_methods.quote:
The analysis of death from all causes (the primary end point)
included all patients, according to the intention-to-treat principle.

analysis_methods.text: Sample size assumptions included placebo mortality 38% and 17% lower risk of death with spironolactone.
analysis_methods.quote:
The sample size was calculated on the basis of the following
assumptions: the mortality rate in the placebo group would be
38 percent, the risk of death would be 17 percent lower in the
spironolactone group than in the placebo group

trial_conduct.quote:
The in-
stitutional review boards or ethics committees of all participating
institutions approved the protocol

trial_conduct.text: Written informed consent was obtained from all patients.
trial_conduct.quote:
and all patients gave written
informed consent.

trial_conduct.text: An independent data and safety monitoring board periodically reviewed results in a blinded fashion.
trial_conduct.quote:
An independent data and safety monitoring board periodically
reviewed the results in a blinded fashion.

trial_conduct.text: Event committees (blinded to treatment) assessed causes of death and reasons for hospitalization.

criticisms.text: The trial was discontinued early after interim analysis showed efficacy.
criticisms.quote:
The trial was discontinued early, after a
mean follow-up period of 24 months, because an in-
terim analysis determined that spironolactone was
efficacious.

criticisms.text: Effectiveness and risks in patients at lower risk than those in this study require further prospective study.
criticisms.quote:
The effectiveness and risks of treatment with spirono-
lactone in patients at lower risk than those in our
study, such as those with less severe heart failure,
will require further prospective study.
